request: mix: 2つのCSVの列ごとのハッシュを比べ変化した列を示す / CSVファイルを1つまたは2つ受け取り（1つなら標準入力と比較せず単独表示）、列ごとにその列の全セルを連結したSHA-256の先頭8桁を計算して、Markdownの表で出力する。列は列名、ファイル1のハッシュ、ファイル2のハッシュ、同じか違うか（same/diff/only-a/only-b）。例: old.csv と new.csv で price列だけ値が変わっていれば、price行に diff、他の列に same と出す。フラグは -n（ハッシュの桁数、既定8）のみ。コマンド名は colhash

spec.name: colhash
spec.summary: colhash prints a Markdown table of per-column SHA-256 prefixes for one CSV file, or compares them between two CSV files.

flags.name: n
flags.help: number of hex characters of each hash (1 to 64)

behavior: B1: Arguments are one or two CSV file paths. Stdin is never read. With 0 or more than 2 file arguments, print "colhash: expected one or two CSV files" and the usage line to stderr, exit 2.
B2: If -n is less than 1 or greater than 64, print "colhash: -n must be between 1 and 64" to stderr, exit 2. Check this before reading any file.

B3: Each file is parsed with encoding/csv (FieldsPerRecord = -1, so rows may differ in length). The first record is the header giving column names; the remaining records are data rows. A file with no records at all has zero columns.

B4: For the column at header index i, the cell is the field at index i of each data row, in row order, or empty if the row is shorter. Fields beyond the header length are ignored. All cells are concatenated with no separator as UTF-8 bytes; the hash is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of that, cut to its first N characters. A column with no data rows hashes the empty string.
B5: If a header name repeats within one file, the second occurrence is named NAME#2, the third NAME#3, and so on; these names are used for matching and printing.

B6: One file: print to stdout the line "| Column | Hash |", the line "| --- | --- |", then one line "| NAME | HASH |" per column in header order. Every line ends with a newline. Zero columns prints just the two header lines.

B7: Two files: print "| Column | File1 hash | File2 hash | Status |", then "| --- | --- | --- | --- |", then one line "| NAME | HASH1 | HASH2 | STATUS |" per column: first all columns of file 1 in its order, then columns present only in file 2 in its order. Columns are matched by name (after B5).

B8: STATUS is same if both hashes are equal, diff if the column is in both files and the hashes differ, only-a if only in file 1, only-b if only in file 2. The hash cell of the file lacking the column is "-".
B9: In printed names, a pipe character is written as \| (backslash then pipe).
B10: If a file cannot be opened or is malformed CSV, print "colhash: FILE: MESSAGE" to stderr, print nothing to stdout, exit 1.
B11: Exit 0 on success, even when the files differ.
